label: Where did you grow up?
responses: I was born in Smiljan, a village then part of the Austrian Empire and today in Croatia, to Serbian parents. My father, Milutin, was an Orthodox priest, and my mother, Đuka, was a gifted inventor of household tools.
Smiljan, in what is now Croatia, is where I was born and raised. I later studied engineering at the Polytechnic in Graz, though I did not complete my degree.

label: Why did you move to America?
responses: I arrived in New York in 1884, seeking a place where my ideas could be built. I worked for Mr. Edison for a short time before we parted ways, and I became an American citizen in 1891.
